data.body:
ORDERING CORRECTION for S3, recorded here as a comment because the epic's description is signed and a text edit would stale its attestation.

The epic's architectural-constraint list says live recovery runs "after configuration snapshot/preflight and exclusive lock/staleness validation but before remote issue fetch, binding walk, differ, or lifecycle mutation." Two parts of that turned out not to hold against the actual spine, and S3's story plan and file impact have been corrected accordingly (S3 was unsigned at the time, so the correction was made before earning its attestation, and the corrected plan then passed review-plan with 0 blocking).

What was verified by reading reconcile.py:
1. `_load_snapshots(ctx)` is called at reconcile.py:222 and internally constructs the binding store (:280), runs the under-lock staleness gate (:281-282), creates the first write-bearing artifact (:286), and performs the FIRST remote issue fetch (:328-333).
2. `bind_operation_runtime` — the immutable operation/config snapshot — is composed at :227, i.e. AFTER `_load_snapshots` returns and therefore AFTER that fetch. So "after the configuration snapshot AND before the remote fetch" is an EMPTY window in the current code.
3. `run_differs()` is invoked at :231, also after the fetch, and the existing `recover_pending_bindings` call inside it (run_differs.py:418) therefore already runs post-fetch. No point inside run_differs.py can precede remote observation.

Resolution: the pre-observation requirement is the load-bearing half, because its stated purpose is to stop an upgraded pass interleaving new liveness evidence with completion. Retirement completion reads only local binding state and has no dependency on the operation config snapshot, so the snapshot conjunct was dropped rather than satisfied; where that snapshot is composed remains RP-04's decision. The invocation therefore lands in reconcile.py immediately after the staleness gate, and run_differs.py needs no edit at all.

Consequence worth flagging for anyone planning further work here: the binding constraint is NOT run_differs.py's 61 lines of headroom, it is reconcile.py's SIX (794 of the 800 cap). So the spine gets a single call line and every guard lives in binding_recovery.py. reconcile.py is also in RP-04 S7.3.a's impact set, so that file is contested.

SEPARATE FINDING, filed as easygoing-tremendous-frogmouth (7851-e06b-9e85-4c9e) discovered_from the S3 story: the existing create-recovery call has NO write-bearing gate, only `if not scoped_ids`, and is handed the real configured transport. So a `preview` or `--mode dry-run` pass performs remote `add_label` / `set_entity_property` writes while `persist=False` suppresses the local save that would have recorded them. The invariant-filing gate immediately beside it composes both axes (`(not persist) or bool(scoped_ids)`), so the omission is asymmetric with its own neighbour. S3 pins this behaviour rather than changing it — S3 T1 carries an explicit AC that the create-recovery gate is unchanged — because it is a behaviour change to anti-duplicate machinery and needs its own plan.
